'''Georg Nagel''' (born 24 August 1953) is a German [[biophysics|biophysicist]] and professor at the Department for [[Neurophysiology]] at the [[University of Würzburg]] in Germany. His research is focused on microbial photoreceptors and the development of [[optogenetic|optogenetic tools]]. In 2026, he was jointly awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]] with [[Karl Deisseroth]]  and[[ Peter Hegemann]] "for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics."<ref name="NobelPrize.org">{{Cite web |title=Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/press-release/ |access-date=2026-10-05 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261005094452/https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/press-release/ |archive-date=2026-10-05 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
{{No sources section|date=October 2026}}
Georg Nagel studied biology and biophysics at the [[University of Konstanz]], Germany. He received his PhD from the [[Goethe University Frankfurt|University of Frankfurt]] in 1988, working at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biophysics]] in Frankfurt. As a postdoc, he worked at [[Yale University]] and [[Rockefeller University]], US.  

==Career==
From 1992 to 2004, Nagel headed an independent research group in the Department of Biophysical Chemistry at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biophysics]] in Frankfurt. Since 2004, he is a professor at the [[University of Würzburg]], Germany, first at the Department for Molecular Plant Physiology and Biophysics, since 2019 at the Department for Neurophysiology.

==Research==
{{primary sources section|date=October 2026}}
[[File:2026-Nobel-Prize-Channelrhodopsin-Hegasy Illustration.png|thumb|350px|Nobel Prize 2026 for the development of optogenetics]]
Georg Nagel, together with [[Peter Hegemann]], is credited with the discovery of [[channelrhodopsin]]s, which opened the new field of [[optogenetics]].<ref>{{Cite Algae|journal=Science|volume=296|issue=5577|pages=2395–2398|doi=10.1126/science.1072068|pmid=12089443|s2cid=206506942}}</ref> Early in 1995, Georg Nagel and [[Ernst Bamberg]] demonstrated that a microbial rhodopsin ([[Bacteriorhodopsin]]), when expressed in animal cells (''[[Xenopus]]'' oocytes), is fully functional and makes the cells light-sensitive.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nagel|first1=Georg|last2=Möckel|first2=Bettina|last3=Büldt|first3=Georg|last4=Bamberg|first4=Ernst|date=1995-12-18|title=Functional expression of bacteriorhodopsin in oocytes allows [[channelrhodopsin-2]] (ChR2) in a mammalian cell line, where illumination with blue light caused a strong depolarization of the membrane potential.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nagel|first1=G.|last2=Szellas|first2=T.|last3=Huhn|first3=W.|last4=Kateriya|first4=S.|last5=Adeishvili|first5=N.|last6=Berthold|first6=P.|last7=Ollig|first7=D.|last8=Hegemann|first8=P.|last9=Bamberg|first9=E.|date=2003-11-25|title=Channelrhodopsin-2, ==Honours and awards==
* 2010 [[Wiley Prize in Biomedical Sciences]], together with Peter Hegemann and Ernst Bamberg<ref>[http://eu.wiley.com/WileyCDA/PressRelease/pressReleaseId-67957.html?print=true Ninth Annual Wiley Prize in Biomedical Sciences Awarded to Dr. Peter Hegemann, Dr. Georg Nagel, and Dr. Ernst Bamberg] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200521080231/https://www.wiley.com//WileyCDA/PressRelease/pressReleaseId-67957.html?print=true%3Fprint%3Dtrue |date=2020-05-21 }} (wiley.com)</ref>
* 2010 Karl Heinz Beckurts Prize, together with Peter Hegemann und Ernst Bamberg<ref>[http://www.beckurts-stiftung.de/preis/preistraeger.html Preisträger] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100704080132/http://www.beckurts-stiftung.de/preis/preistraeger.html |date=2010-07-04 }} of the Karl Heinz Beckurts Foundation (beckurts-stiftung.de)</ref>
* 2012 Zülch Prize<ref name="i991">{{cite web | title=International Prize for Translational Neuroscience | website=Max-Planck-Gesellschaft | date=18 August 2026 | url=https://www.mpg.de/preise/international-prize-for-translational-neuroscience | language=de | access-date=5 October 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260729134139/https://www.mpg.de/preise/international-prize-for-translational-neuroscience | archive-date=29 July 2026 | url-status=live}}</ref>
* 2013 [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jeantet.ch/en/prix-louis-jeantet/laureats/2018-en/professeurs-peter-hegemann-et-georg-nagel/ |title=Louis-Jeantet Prize |access-date=2018-12-19 |archive-date=2020-03-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327010101/https://www.jeantet.ch/en/prix-louis-jeantet/laureats/2013-en/professeurs-peter-hegemann-et-georg-nagel/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> together with Peter Hegemann
* 2013 The Brain Prize,<ref name="brain">[http://www.thebrainprize.org/flx/prize_winners/peter_hegemann/ Peter Hegemann] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151230091155/http://www.thebrainprize.org/flx/prize_winners/peter_hegemann/ |date=2015-12-30 }} thebrainprize.org</ref> awarded by the ''Grete Lundbeck European Brain Research Foundation''
* 2015 selected as Member of the European Molecular Biology Organization (EMBO)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Georg Nagel |url=https://people.embo.org/profile/georg-nagel |access-date=5 October 2026 |website=[[European Molecular Biology Organization|EMBO]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251109061502/https://people.embo.org/profile/georg-nagel |archive-date=9 November 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="o183">{{cite web | title=Hohe Auszeichnung für Georg Nagel | website=Universität Würzburg | date=27 August 2023 | url=https://www.biozentrum.uni-wuerzburg.de/bot1/nachrichten/single/news/hohe-auszeichnung-fuer-georg-nagel-2/ | language=de | access-date=5 October 2026}}</ref>
* 2019 [[Rumford Prize]] for "extraordinary contributions related to the invention and refinement of optogenetics," with [[Ernst Bamberg]], [[Edward Boyden|Ed Boyden]], [[Karl Deisseroth]], [[Peter Hegemann]], and [[Gero Miesenböck]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/news/rumford-prize-optogenetics|title=Rumford Prize Awarded for the Invention and Refinement of Optogenetics|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en|access-date=2019-03-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206083834/https://www.amacad.org/news/rumford-prize-optogenetics|archive-date=2021-02-06|url-status=live}}</ref>
* 2020 [[Shaw Prize]] in Life Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.shawprize.org/prizes/life-science-medicine |title=Shaw Prize 2020 |access-date=2020-05-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200810220336/https://www.shawprize.org/prizes/life-science-medicine |archive-date=2020-08-10 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2026 [[Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine]]<ref name="NobelPrize.org" />

Nagel's 2026 Nobel award recognised discoveries made at the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics in Frankfurt. The Nobel Assembly highlighted his work with Peter Hegemann in identifying the algal protein channelrhodopsin, which made cells sensitive to blue light. The prize was shared equally with Hegemann and Karl Deisseroth, who developed its use in controlling nerve cells.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 – Press release |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/press-release/ |website=NobelPrize.org |date=5 October 2026 |access-date=10 October 2026}}</ref>
